back.body: Body → RIGHT atrium → right ventricle → LUNGS (picks up oxygen) → LEFT atrium → left ventricle → BODY · Valves keep it one-way · Left ventricle is thickest because it supplies the whole body, not just next door · LEFT fails → backs up into the LUNGS · RIGHT fails → backs up into the BODY (ankles, neck veins)
back.why_it_matters: Follow one drop round the circuit and heart failure stops being a list to memorise.

back.body: The heart makes its OWN electricity — no nerve from the brain needed · SA node = natural pacemaker, fires fastest · AV node DELAYS the impulse so the atria can finish emptying · Then down through the ventricles, which contract · Lower sites take over if the one above fails, each SLOWER · A rhythm on the monitor does NOT prove a pulse
back.why_it_matters: The monitor watches the wiring. Your fingers watch the plumbing.

back.body: Cardiac output = HEART RATE x STROKE VOLUME · Stroke volume = what leaves per beat, set by PRELOAD (how full before the squeeze) and AFTERLOAD (what it pushes against) · Blood loss → preload down → stroke volume down → body raises RATE to compensate · That is why TACHYCARDIA is an early shock sign, before BP moves · Too fast = no filling time = output falls
back.why_it_matters: A normal heart rate proves nothing. It is one of two terms.

back.body: See the numbers card: output = rate x stroke volume; stroke volume is per-beat ejection; preload is filling; afterload is resistance; tachycardia is the early compensation and appears long before blood pressure changes.
back.why_it_matters: Everything in shock follows from this one equation.

back.body: The muscle gets NOTHING from blood inside the chambers · Coronary arteries are the FIRST branches off the aorta, just past the left ventricle · They fill mainly BETWEEN beats — contraction squeezes them shut · So a very fast rate cuts the heart's own supply · A blockage starves the muscle downstream = heart attack · Which vessel decides which territory
back.why_it_matters: More beats, yes — but less time between them, and that is when the heart drinks.
